specification: Implement a FIFO inventory ledger as the package fifo, consisting of three editable modules (fifo/lots.py, fifo/costing.py, fifo/ledger.py) plus an empty fifo/__init__.py that must not be edited. All money is in integer cents. fifo/lots.py defines class Lot(lot_id, unit_cost, qty), which stores those three values as attributes of the same names, and the functions total_qty(lots), consume(lots, qty) and restore(lots, lot_id, unit_cost, qty). A lots argument is a list of Lot objects kept in ascending lot_id order, which is also oldest-first order. total_qty returns the sum of qty over the list. consume(lots, qty), where qty is a positive int, removes qty units from the front of the list, oldest lot first, mutating the list and its Lot objects in place: a lot whose quantity reaches zero is removed from the list, a partly used lot stays with its reduced qty. It returns a list of (lot_id, taken, unit_cost) tuples, one per lot touched, in consumption order. If total_qty(lots) < qty it raises ValueError and leaves lots unchanged. restore(lots, lot_id, unit_cost, qty) puts qty units back: if a lot with that lot_id is in the list, its qty grows by qty; otherwise a new Lot(lot_id, unit_cost, qty) is inserted so that the list stays in ascending lot_id order. fifo/costing.py defines total_cost(taken), which takes a list of (lot_id, taken, unit_cost) tuples and returns the sum of taken * unit_cost, and average_cost(total, qty), which takes a nonnegative int total and a positive int qty and returns the nearest integer to the exact ratio total/qty; ties choose the larger integer. fifo/ledger.py defines class Ledger, which starts empty, with these methods. receive(sku, qty, unit_cost) appends a new lot for sku to the end of that sku's lots and returns the new lot id; lot ids are 1, 2, 3, ... across the whole ledger regardless of sku. issue(sku, qty) takes qty units of sku from its oldest lots using the rules of consume and returns a dict with the keys 'issue_id' (1, 2, 3, ... across the whole ledger), 'cost' (total_cost of the units taken), 'unit_cost' (average_cost of that cost and qty) and 'lots' (a list of (lot_id, taken) tuples in consumption order). An unknown sku, or a sku with fewer than qty units in stock, raises ValueError. return_items(issue_id, qty) puts qty units of an earlier issue back into stock and returns a dict with the keys 'credit' (the sum, over the units put back, of the unit cost of the lot each unit goes back to) and 'restored' (a list of (lot_id, count) tuples in the order the lots were restored). Units go back to the lots that the issue took them from, walking those lots from the last one the issue consumed to the first one; each lot absorbs at most the quantity the issue took from it minus the quantity already returned to it by earlier calls, and a lot that is no longer in stock is recreated with its original unit cost according to the rules of restore. An unknown issue_id, or a qty larger than the number of units of that issue not yet returned, raises ValueError. on_hand(sku) returns the units in stock (0 for an unknown sku), value(sku) returns the sum of qty * unit_cost over the sku's lots (0 for an unknown sku), and lots(sku) returns a list of (lot_id, qty, unit_cost) tuples in FIFO order (an empty list for an unknown sku). Validation in every public Ledger method: check the arguments from left to right, and for each argument check its type before its value, before looking at ledger state. sku must be a built-in str, and qty, unit_cost and issue_id must be built-in ints; bool and other subclasses are rejected. A wrong type raises TypeError. sku must be nonempty, qty and issue_id must be at least 1, and unit_cost must be at least 0; a violation raises ValueError. Any call that raises leaves the ledger exactly as it was, including the counters used for lot ids and issue ids. Exception messages are not specified.
